findings.description: The new housekeeping clause `^Merge pull request #[0-9]+ from [^ ]+/chore/` is evaluated before the R-005 release-merge clause (`from [^ ]+/release/`) further down in the same function. `[^ ]+` spans any number of path segments, so the clause matches a `chore` segment anywhere in the branch path, not only the first segment after the owner. A release merge whose branch path contains a `chore` segment (e.g. `0xHoneyJar/release/chore/v2.1.0` or `0xHoneyJar/chore/release/v2.1.0`) therefore now classifies `other` instead of `cycle`. That is the exact misrouting shape behind the documented R-005 incident (PR #1201, release merge routed to `other`, auto-tagged v1.195.1). The reviewer's dry run says the `other` path today prepares a candidate without tagging, so the present impact is skipped cycle-only phases rather than a wrong tag; the orchestrator was not available in the audit material, so that claim was not independently verified. None of PCT-T28..T36 pins the chore-vs-release precedence, so a regression here would be silent.
findings.failure_mode: A release-branch merge whose path contains a `chore` segment is routed to the Bugfix-or-Other job and skips the cycle release phases (CHANGELOG, GT, RTFM, Release run). If the `other` path ever regains automatic tagging, the R-005 wrong-PATCH-tag incident recurs for that merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the branch clause to the first segment after the owner: `^Merge pull request #[0-9]+ from [^ /]+/chore/`, so only `owner/chore/...` branches match. Alternatively move the release-merge clause above the housekeeping clause. In either case add a PCT case such as `Merge pull request #N from org/release/chore/v2.1.0 — ...` asserting `cycle`, and one for `org/chore/cycle-NNN-archive` asserting `other`, to pin the precedence.

If the `other` path ever regains automatic tagging, the R-005 wrong-PATCH-tag incident recurs for that merge.
